text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: Elevated CUDA OOMs and KV-cache fragmentation detected on prod-serving pool. Pager fired at 1847654321. Auto-throttle engaged.

marta: seeing a spike in arena fragmentation on rr-gpu-1..5, allocator metrics show free arenas not returning.

tj: confirmed, continuous-batching token sizes spiked around 11:07 UTC, KV hit-rate dropped. Suspect prefix/KV eviction thrash. :warning:

sophia: any customer-facing errors?

ryan: yes, a handful of in-flight requests returned 429s and a couple latency > 3s. We have a reduction in throughput per node. Impact: ~2% of requests; more for long-seq workloads.

oncall-nick: I'm paged and taking lead. Starting triage — what's the quickest mitigation to reduce OOM pressure?

marta: short term: reduce continuous batching window, force KV compaction, and lower per-request max_tokens for canaries.

tj: I can push a hotfix to routing to set batching.max_batch_delay=4ms -> 1ms for the affected pools, and set batch.size_cap=64 -> 32. That should reduce combined KV working set.

infra-bot: Deploy plan posted: https://playbooks.internal/runbook/kv-arena - please ack for canary.

oncall-nick: ack. Running canary change on rr-gpu-1 first.

sophia: I'll open a customer-impact note in status page draft and loop in support.

ryan: command I ran for quick compaction on node: ```sudo pkill -USR1 kv_compactor && python3 tools/kv_compact.py --node rr-gpu-1 --force``` compaction freed ~18% arena usage on that node.

marta: nice, but compaction is slow cluster-wide. Need allocator-level change. There's an allocator param (arena_retire_threshold) we can tune to be more aggressive returning memory to cuda.

tj: I'll roll a 2-line hotpatch to runtime config to set arena_retire_threshold=0.6 -> 0.3 for the impacted pools. Preparing patch now.

incident-bot: ACTION REQUIRED: If hotpatch fails, fallback is to spin new instances with fresh allocator and migrate traffic. Estimated time to spin: 6-8 minutes per instance.

oncall-nick: patch applied to rr-gpu-1..3. Monitoring memory metrics.

marta: metrics show fragmentation down 12% on rr-gpu-1 and OOM count dropped to 0 on the node. Throughput stabilized.

sophia: status update: customer-facing error rate reduced, posting to status.redwood.ai. Notifying affected customers via support.

ryan: I'm seeing an odd regression on one of the canaries where latency jitter increased. Reverting batch.size_cap on that node only.

tj: ack, revert applied, canary looks stable again. We'll keep reduced delay but restore size to avoid perf cliff for medium-seq requests.

marta: action items summary: 1) temporary config: batching delay -> 1ms for affected pools (done), 2) hotpatch allocator retire threshold (done on canaries), 3) run cluster-wide compaction over off-peak (scheduled), 4) follow-up: implement KV slab coalescing in allocator (owner: tj), 5) run retro.

oncall-nick: handing off to night oncall @ryan for monitoring. I'll join overlap at 00:30 UTC.

ryan: taking over. I've subscribed to fragmentation dashboards and set an alert for fragmentation > 20% for any node.

infra-bot: postmortem draft created: https://docs.internal/incidents/1847654321-kv-arena-defrag-draft. Assign owners and timelines.

sophia: good job team. Please add precise customer list and elapsed minutes for SLAs in the postmortem.

marta: will add allocator heuristics and perf graphs. tj, can you estimate ETA for slab coalescing PR?

tj: aiming for PR in 3 business days, can ship a safer config option + more aggressive compaction as incremental steps earlier.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: hotpatch + compaction reduced OOMs and fragmentation to baseline on all canaries by 1847654720. Monitoring continues. :white_check_mark:

ryan: logging final note: root cause = allocator retention heuristics combined with sudden continuous-batch size spike from an experimental routing rollout. We'll add a conservative rollout gate for batch config changes.

sophia: closing channel for now, will reopen if metrics cross thresholds. Thanks everyone. :tada:
